_README: route_type for stages where PCS's own metadata describes the wrong kind of race.
ingest derives route_type from the stage page: is_ttt from the page structure, then
PCS's TitleTT marker, then detect_route_type() on the profile icon and 'Won how'.
All three read PCS. When PCS itself is wrong about what kind of race was ridden,
there is nothing in the scrape to correct it from, and a re-scrape reproduces the
Lives outside the DB on purpose. ingest_race.py deletes and re-inserts a whole
edition, and only vertical_meters, profile_score, distance_km, cancelled and
source_slug survive that. route_type does NOT, so a direct DB patch is reverted by
the next re-ingest with nothing to say it had gone.
Keyed by PCS source_slug, not by stage_number: the slug names the PAGE whose
metadata is wrong, and it is stable across the renumbering that split days cause
(the DB stage 3 of the 1992 Vuelta is the page stage-2b). stage_number is carried in
the entry for humans and for cross-checking, never as the lookup key.
stage_type follows route_type automatically ('itt' for TT/TTT, else 'road').
Every entry needs a source. This file overrides a real source with another real
source; it is not a place to record a hunch.
Race keys are the DB race name ("Giro d'Italia"), matching stage_notes.json.

stage-8a.note: Not a time trial. A 'Giri-sprint': a 5 km circuit at Foggia ridden 9 times, with time bonuses to the first three riders across the line on lap 1 and the first four on lap 9. One of five such stages in the 1980s. PCS reports 'Won how: Time trial', which is what produced route_type='TT'. Wikipedia types it a plain stage; Allocchio won it from the bunch and the DB already has him at rank 1 on 53:52 with the peloton on the same time, so the 171 shared times are correct and only the label was wrong. The tell is in our own numbers: 45 km at 50.1 km/h, Foggia to Foggia, in 1985 - faster than Moser's hour record, and no time trial of that length has been ridden at that speed.
